FICTIONAL TEST DOCUMENT. Deepa Nair versus City Hospital. The complainant alleged medical negligence after a surgical sponge was left inside her abdomen during an appendix operation, requiring a second surgery. The hospital argued that complications are an accepted risk of surgery. The commission held that leaving a foreign object inside a patient is negligence per se, because it does not happen in the ordinary course when proper care is taken, and the burden shifts to the hospital to explain it. The hospital offered no explanation. Compensation of six lakh rupees was awarded for the second surgery, pain and suffering and loss of income, with interest at nine percent per annum from the date of the complaint until payment.
